notes: Linker form 'isang' before nouns: isang tao. Tagalog numbers count things; Spanish numbers do time, money, age.

examples.tl: Isa lang ang kailangan ko.
examples.en: I only need one.

examples.tl: Isang order ng sisig, please.
examples.en: One order of sisig, please.

notes: Linker form 'dalawang': dalawang kilo. 'Kaming dalawa' = the two of us.

examples.tl: Dalawang kilo ng manggang hilaw, kuya.
examples.en: Two kilos of green mango, kuya.

examples.tl: Kaming dalawa lang ang pupunta.
examples.en: Only the two of us are going.

notes: Linker form 'tatlong'.

examples.tl: Tatlo kaming magkakapatid.
examples.en: There are three of us siblings.

examples.tl: Tatlong araw na akong walang tulog.
examples.en: I have gone three days without sleep.

notes: Linker form 'apat na' (ends in consonant, so 'na' not '-ng').

examples.tl: Apat na tao, may table pa ba?
examples.en: Four people, is there still a table?

notes: Linker form 'limang'. For five pesos people say 'singko' (Spanish), not 'limang piso'.

examples.tl: Limang piraso ng pandesal, please.
examples.en: Five pieces of pandesal, please.

notes: Linker form 'anim na'.

examples.tl: Anim na buwan na ako sa Makati.
examples.en: I have been in Makati for six months.

notes: Linker form 'pitong'.

examples.tl: Pitong araw sa isang linggo.
examples.en: Seven days in a week.

notes: Linker form 'walong'.

examples.tl: Walong oras ang shift ko.
examples.en: My shift is eight hours.

notes: Linker form 'siyam na'.

examples.tl: Siyam na taon na silang kasal.
examples.en: They have been married nine years.

notes: Linker form 'sampung'. For ten pesos say 'diyes'.

examples.tl: Sampung minuto lang, malapit na ako.
examples.en: Just ten minutes, I am almost there.

notes: labing- + unit = 11 to 19: labindalawa (12), labintatlo (13), labing-apat (14)...

examples.tl: Labing-isang taon na ang anak niya.
examples.en: Her kid is eleven years old now.

notes: Tens: dalawampu, tatlumpu, apatnapu, limampu, animnapu... In money/age people usually say 'bente' instead.

examples.tl: Dalawampung tao ang pumunta sa party.
examples.en: Twenty people came to the party.

notes: Also 'sandaan'. For P100 people just say 'one hundred' or 'isang daan'; 'syento' mostly in dos syentos, tres syentos.

examples.tl: Isang daan lang 'to? Ang mura!
examples.en: This is only a hundred? So cheap!

notes: P1,000 is 'isang libo' or 'one thousand'; 'mil' shows up in 'dos mil', 'singko mil'.

examples.tl: Isang libo ang budget ko sa grocery ngayong linggo.
examples.en: My grocery budget this week is a thousand.

notes: Spanish-derived numbers are used for clock time, prices, and age. 'Uno' alone is rare except 'ala-una' (1 o'clock) and the top grade 1.0 in school.

examples.tl: Nakakuha siya ng uno sa Math.
examples.en: She got a 1.0 (highest grade) in Math.

notes: Used in time (alas-dos), money (dos syentos, dos mil), and lotto/jersey numbers. Counting objects still uses 'dalawa'.

examples.tl: Dos mil ang renta ng parking kada buwan.
examples.en: Parking rent is two thousand a month.

notes: alas-tres = 3 o'clock; tres syentos = 300.

examples.tl: Tres syentos lang ang damit sa ukay.
examples.en: The shirt at the thrift stall is only three hundred.

notes: alas-kwatro = 4 o'clock.

examples.tl: Uwian na namin ng alas-kwatro.
examples.en: Our dismissal is at four.

notes: The everyday word for five pesos and 5 o'clock. 'Singko' also = the P5 coin.

examples.tl: May singko ka? Para exact ang bayad sa jeep.
examples.en: Do you have five pesos? So the jeep fare is exact.

notes: alas-sais = 6 o'clock, the usual uwian/meetup time.

examples.tl: Alas-sais ng gabi tayo magkita sa Ayala.
examples.en: Let's meet at six in the evening at Ayala.

notes: alas-siyete = 7 o'clock.

examples.tl: Alas-siyete pa ang flight, chill lang.
examples.en: The flight is not until seven, relax.

notes: alas-otso = 8 o'clock.

examples.tl: Alas-otso ng umaga ang pasok ko.
examples.en: My work starts at eight in the morning.

notes: alas-nuwebe = 9 o'clock.

examples.tl: Bukas ang mall mula alas-diyes hanggang alas-nuwebe.
examples.en: The mall is open from ten until nine.

notes: Ten pesos = 'diyes'. alas-diyes = 10 o'clock.

examples.tl: Diyes lang ang dagdag kung may extra rice.
examples.en: It is only ten pesos more with extra rice.

notes: alas-dose = noon or midnight. Eleven is 'onse' (alas-onse).

examples.tl: Alas-dose na, lunch tayo.
examples.en: It is twelve already, let's have lunch.

notes: alas-onse = 11 o'clock. Slang: 'ini-onse' = to cheat someone, as in 'na-onse ako'.

examples.tl: Alas-onse pa ang check-in, maaga pa tayo.
examples.en: Check-in is not until eleven, we are early.

notes: Also the 15th (payday: 'kinse'), P15, and quarter past: alas-dos kinse.

examples.tl: Sahod sa kinse, tapos ulit sa katapusan.
examples.en: Payday on the 15th, then again at month end.

notes: Twenty pesos is always 'bente', never 'dalawampung piso'. 'Bente singko' = 25.

examples.tl: Bente isang tumpok ang kamatis.
examples.en: Tomatoes are twenty pesos a pile.

examples.tl: Bente lang ang pamasahe sa jeep hanggang Guadalupe.
examples.en: The jeep fare to Guadalupe is only twenty.

notes: Also used for age: 'trenta na ako'.

examples.tl: Trenta na siya pero mukhang bente pa.
examples.en: She is thirty but still looks twenty.

notes: 'Kwarenta y singko' = 45, as in 'alas-dos kwarenta y singko'.

examples.tl: Kwarenta pesos ang bottled water sa loob ng mall.
examples.en: Bottled water inside the mall is forty pesos.

notes: Fifty pesos = 'singkwenta'.

examples.tl: Singkwenta ang isang kilo ng kamote ngayon.
examples.en: A kilo of sweet potato is fifty right now.

examples.tl: Sisenta na ang tatay ko pero nag-gym pa.
examples.en: My dad is sixty but still goes to the gym.

examples.tl: Setenta ang ulam na may kanin sa karinderya.
examples.en: The meal with rice at the eatery is seventy.

examples.tl: Otsenta pesos ang isang order ng lumpia.
examples.en: One order of lumpia is eighty pesos.

examples.tl: Nobenta na si Lola pero malakas pa.
examples.en: Grandma is ninety but still strong.

notes: Used in dos syentos (200), tres syentos (300), kinyentos (500). P100 alone is 'isang daan' or 'one hundred'.

examples.tl: Dos syentos singkwenta ang Grab papuntang BGC.
examples.en: The Grab to BGC is two hundred fifty.

notes: dos mil = 2,000; singko mil = 5,000; diyes mil = 10,000. 'Isang libo' or 'one thousand' for 1,000.

examples.tl: Singko mil ang deposit sa condo.
examples.en: The condo deposit is five thousand.

notes: 'Una' = first; 'unang beses' = first time; 'nauna' = went first. Ordinals: una, ikalawa, ikatlo...

examples.tl: Unang beses ko sa Palawan!
examples.en: My first time in Palawan!

notes: 'Pangalawa' is the everyday spoken form; 'ikalawa' is more formal/written.

examples.tl: Pangalawang beses na 'to na na-late ka.
examples.en: This is the second time you have been late.

notes: Question word 'how many'; also 'a few': 'ilang araw' = a few days / how many days.

examples.tl: Ilan kayo? Para ma-reserve ko ang table.
examples.en: How many of you? So I can reserve the table.

examples.tl: Ilang araw ka sa Cebu?
examples.en: How many days are you in Cebu?

notes: 'Lahat ng' before nouns; 'kayong lahat' = all of you. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much altogether?

examples.tl: Magkano lahat, ate?
examples.en: How much is everything, ate?

examples.tl: Lahat kami na-stuck sa traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: All of us got stuck in traffic on EDSA.

notes: 'Kalahating kilo' = half a kilo; 'kalahating oras' = half an hour. Also just 'half' in Taglish.

examples.tl: Kalahating kilo lang ng baboy, ate.
examples.en: Just half a kilo of pork, ate.

examples.tl: Hati tayo, kalahati sa'yo kalahati sa'kin.
examples.en: Let's split it, half for you, half for me.

notes: 'Isang pares ng sapatos'. Also the beef stew 'pares' at roadside eateries, unrelated meaning.

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng dalawang pares ng medyas sa Divisoria.
examples.en: I bought two pairs of socks in Divisoria.

notes: Eggs are sold by the dozen or by the tray; 'kalahating dosena' = half a dozen.

examples.tl: Isang dosenang itlog, magkano?
examples.en: How much for a dozen eggs?

notes: 'Anong oras?' = what time? 'Isang oras' = one hour. 'Walang oras' = no time. 'May oras ka ba?' = do you have time?

examples.tl: Anong oras ang pasok mo bukas?
examples.en: What time do you start work tomorrow?

examples.tl: Dalawang oras ako sa traffic kanina.
examples.en: I was in traffic for two hours earlier.

notes: Answer with Spanish numbers: 'Alas-tres na.' Add 'ba' for a softer question: 'Anong oras na ba?'

examples.tl: Anong oras na? Baka na-late na tayo.
examples.en: What time is it? We might be late already.
examples.taglish: Anong oras na? Shoot, late na tayo.

notes: Only 1 o'clock uses 'ala-'; all others use 'alas-' (alas-dos, alas-tres...). From Spanish 'a la una'.

examples.tl: Ala-una ng hapon ang meeting natin.
examples.en: Our meeting is at one in the afternoon.

notes: Pattern: alas- + Spanish number. Minutes follow directly: alas-dos diyes = 2:10, alas-dos trenta = 2:30.

examples.tl: Kita tayo sa Glorietta ng alas-dos.
examples.en: Let's meet at Glorietta at two.

notes: 'y medya' = :30. Young people often just say 'three thirty'. Both are fine.

examples.tl: Alas-tres y medya pa ang check-out, may oras pa tayo.
examples.en: Check-out is not until half past three, we still have time.

notes: From Spanish 'y media'. 'Alas-sais y medya' = 6:30. Alternative: 'alas-sais trenta'.

examples.tl: Alas-otso y medya ang call time, wag ma-late.
examples.en: Call time is eight thirty, don't be late.

notes: Older/less common pattern: 'alas-singko menos kinse' = 4:45. Most people now say 'kwarenta y singko' or 'four forty-five'.

examples.tl: Alas-singko menos kinse na, tara na.
examples.en: It is quarter to five, let's go.

notes: Attach after the hour: alas-siyete ng umaga. 'Ng' here is pronounced 'nang'.

examples.tl: Alas-sais ng umaga ang alarm ko pero alas-siyete ako gumigising.
examples.en: My alarm is at six in the morning but I wake up at seven.

notes: Roughly 1 PM to about 6 PM. 'Alas-dos ng hapon' = 2 PM.

examples.tl: Dumating ang Lalamove ng alas-kwatro ng hapon.
examples.en: The Lalamove arrived at four in the afternoon.

notes: From about 6 PM onward. 'Alas-nuwebe ng gabi' = 9 PM.

examples.tl: Umuwi ako ng alas-onse ng gabi galing BGC.
examples.en: I got home from BGC at eleven at night.

notes: 'Tanghalian' = lunch. 'Tanghali na!' = it is late in the morning already (you overslept).

examples.tl: Tanghali na, gising na!
examples.en: It is noon already, wake up!

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa labas pag tanghali.
examples.en: It is so hot outside at midday.

notes: From 'hati' (half) + 'gabi'. Many say 'twelve midnight' or 'alas-dose ng gabi'.

examples.tl: Hatinggabi na nakauwi ang kapatid ko galing sa party.
examples.en: My sibling got home from the party at midnight.

notes: Roughly 1 to 5 AM. 'Alas-tres ng madaling-araw' = 3 AM.

examples.tl: Alas-kwatro ng madaling-araw ang flight ko, kaya Grab na lang.
examples.en: My flight is at four in the morning, so I'll just take a Grab.

notes: 'Alas-dose ng tanghali' = noon; 'alas-dose ng gabi' or 'hatinggabi' = midnight.

examples.tl: Alas-dose ng tanghali ang lunch break namin.
examples.en: Our lunch break is at twelve noon.

notes: 'Mga' before a time or number = approximately: 'mga alas-sais', 'mga bente tao'. Very common when setting meetups.

examples.tl: Mga alas-siyete ako makakarating, traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: I'll arrive around seven, there is traffic on EDSA.
examples.taglish: Mga alas-siyete ako, traffic sa EDSA eh.

notes: 'Bago mag-alas-otso' = before 8 o'clock; 'bago mag-Pasko' = before Christmas; 'bago mag-umaga' = before morning.

examples.tl: Umuwi ka bago mag-alas-diyes, may curfew sa condo.
examples.en: Come home before ten, the condo has a curfew.

notes: 'Pagkatapos ng trabaho' = after work. Spoken often shortened to 'tapos'.

examples.tl: Pagkatapos ng trabaho, gym muna ako.
examples.en: After work, I hit the gym first.

examples.tl: Pagkatapos ng alas-sais, free na ako.
examples.en: After six, I'm free.

notes: Taglish often uses 'minutes': 'five minutes lang'. Tagalog number + 'minuto': limang minuto.

examples.tl: Limang minuto na lang, nasa Buendia na ako.
examples.en: Just five more minutes, I'm on Buendia already.

examples.tl: Ilang segundo lang, mag-lo-load pa ang GCash.
examples.en: Just a few seconds, GCash is still loading.

examples.tl: Kalahating oras ang biyahe pag walang traffic, pero bihira 'yon.
examples.en: The trip is half an hour without traffic, but that's rare.

notes: Short way to ask what time the plan is. Answer: 'Mga alas-sais?' Follow with 'Saan tayo?' (where?).

examples.tl: Anong oras tayo bukas? Saan tayo magkikita?
examples.en: What time are we tomorrow? Where do we meet?
examples.taglish: Anong oras tayo bukas? Sa Greenbelt na lang?

notes: 'Ngayon na' = right now. 'Ngayong araw' = today; 'ngayong gabi' = tonight; 'ngayong linggo' = this week.

examples.tl: Busy ako ngayon, mamaya na lang.
examples.en: I'm busy now, maybe later.

examples.tl: Ngayong gabi ba 'yung dinner?
examples.en: Is the dinner tonight?

notes: Earlier the same day. 'Kaninang umaga' = this morning (past). 'Kanina lang' = just a while ago.

examples.tl: Kumain na ako kanina, salamat.
examples.en: I already ate earlier, thanks.

examples.tl: Umulan nang malakas kanina sa Makati.
examples.en: It rained hard earlier in Makati.

notes: Later the same day. 'Mamayang gabi' = tonight (later). 'Mamaya na' = later, not now. Also 'baka mamaya' = maybe later.

examples.tl: Mamaya na ako mag-reply, nasa meeting ako.
examples.en: I'll reply later, I'm in a meeting.

examples.tl: Inuman mamayang gabi sa Poblacion?
examples.en: Drinks tonight in Poblacion?

notes: Stress matters: BU-kas = tomorrow; bu-KAS = open. 'Bukas ng umaga' = tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Bukas na lang natin tapusin, pagod na ako.
examples.en: Let's just finish it tomorrow, I'm tired.

notes: 'Kahapon ng gabi' = last night (also 'kagabi'). 'Kahapon lang' = just yesterday.

examples.tl: Nag-Grab ako kahapon kasi umuulan.
examples.en: I took a Grab yesterday because it was raining.

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng ulan kagabi, hindi ako nakatulog.
examples.en: The rain was so loud last night, I couldn't sleep.

notes: From 'dalawa' (two): two days ago. Compare 'sa makalawa' = the day after tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kamakalawa pa ako nag-order, wala pa rin ang package.
examples.en: I ordered the day before yesterday and the package still isn't here.

notes: 'Sa' marks future time: sa Lunes, sa susunod na linggo, sa makalawa.

examples.tl: Sa makalawa ang kaarawan ni Mama, bili tayo ng cake.
examples.en: Mom's birthday is the day after tomorrow, let's buy a cake.

notes: 'Noon' = past 'then'. 'Noong' marks past time: noong Lunes, noong bata ako, noong 2019.

examples.tl: Noong bata ako, walang Grab, jeep lang.
examples.en: When I was a kid, there was no Grab, just jeeps.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang renta noon.
examples.en: Rent was cheaper back then.

notes: 'Dati' = formerly/used to; 'dating' = former/ex: 'dating boss ko'. 'Dati rati' = in the old days.

examples.tl: Dati nakatira ako sa Pasig, ngayon sa Makati na.
examples.en: I used to live in Pasig, now I'm in Makati.

notes: 'Palagi' and 'parati' are the same. 'Lagi ka bang late?' Often with 'na lang': 'lagi na lang traffic'.

examples.tl: Lagi na lang may traffic sa EDSA pag Biyernes.
examples.en: There's always traffic on EDSA on Fridays.

examples.tl: Lagi akong nag-aalmusal ng pandesal.
examples.en: I always have pandesal for breakfast.

notes: Root 'dalas' (frequency). 'Mas madalas' = more often; 'madalas ba?' = is it often?

examples.tl: Madalas akong mag-order sa Grab Food pag weekend.
examples.en: I often order on Grab Food on weekends.

notes: 'Minsan' = sometimes or one time. 'Minsan lang' = only once / only sometimes. 'Paminsan-minsan' = once in a while.

examples.tl: Minsan nag-jeep ako, minsan nag-Grab, depende sa ulan.
examples.en: Sometimes I take the jeep, sometimes Grab, depending on the rain.

examples.tl: Paminsan-minsan lang ako umiinom, pag may okasyon.
examples.en: I only drink once in a while, when there's an occasion.

notes: Also an adjective: 'bihira 'yon' = that's rare.

examples.tl: Bihira akong magluto, mas madalas take-out.
examples.en: I rarely cook, more often take-out.

notes: Formal/literary. In speech people say 'hindi... kahit kailan' or just 'never' in Taglish: 'never akong na-late'.

examples.tl: Hindi kailanman ako sumakay sa MRT pag rush hour.
examples.en: I never ride the MRT during rush hour.
examples.taglish: Never akong sumakay ng MRT pag rush hour.

notes: With 'hindi' = never: 'Hindi ako kahit kailan nag-bike sa EDSA.' Alone = whenever you like.

examples.tl: Kahit kailan ka pwedeng dumalaw, open lagi ang bahay.
examples.en: You can visit anytime, the house is always open.

notes: Often doubled for emphasis: 'agad-agad'. Goes after the verb: 'umalis agad'.

examples.tl: Nag-reply siya agad, buti pa siya.
examples.en: She replied right away, good for her.

examples.tl: Pag umulan, baha agad sa España.
examples.en: When it rains, España floods immediately.

notes: 'Saglit lang' = just a sec. 'Saglit' alone works as 'hold on'.

examples.tl: Saglit lang, kukuha lang ako ng tubig.
examples.en: Just a sec, I'll just get some water.

notes: 'Sandali' is slightly more formal than 'saglit'. 'Sandali!' = wait!

examples.tl: Sandali, hindi ko pa nakikita ang message mo.
examples.en: Hold on, I haven't seen your message yet.

notes: What you say to a guard, cashier or on the phone when you need a second.

examples.tl: Sandali lang po, hinahanap ko ang ID ko.
examples.en: Just a moment, I'm looking for my ID.

notes: Pure Taglish and extremely common in texting and speech. 'Wait lang ha' softens it.

examples.tl: Wait lang, pinapa-load ko pa ang GCash ko.
examples.en: Hang on, I'm still topping up my GCash.

notes: 'Maaga pa' = it's still early. 'Nang maaga' = early (adverb). 'Maagang-maaga' = very early.

examples.tl: Maaga pa, alas-singko pa lang.
examples.en: It's still early, it's only five.

examples.tl: Umalis ako nang maaga para iwas traffic.
examples.en: I left early to avoid traffic.

notes: Everyday Manila speech uses English 'late': 'na-late ako', 'late na'. Tagalog 'nahuli ako' is understood but less common for lateness.

examples.tl: Sorry, na-late ako, sobrang traffic sa Ayala.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late, traffic on Ayala was terrible.

examples.tl: Late na, tulog na tayo.
examples.en: It's late, let's sleep.

notes: 'Huling biyahe' = last trip; 'sa huli' = in the end; 'nahuli' = was late or was caught. 'Last' is also used in Taglish.

examples.tl: Anong oras ang huling biyahe ng MRT?
examples.en: What time is the last MRT trip?

examples.tl: Nahuli ako sa meeting kasi bumaha.
examples.en: I was late to the meeting because it flooded.

notes: English 'on time' is the normal spoken form. Formal Tagalog 'nasa oras' appears mostly in writing.

examples.tl: Bihirang on time ang bus, kaya maaga ako umaalis.
examples.en: The bus is rarely on time, so I leave early.

notes: 'Linggo' = week AND Sunday (capitalized). 'Isang linggo' = one week; 'ngayong linggo' = this week.

examples.tl: Isang linggo na akong hindi nag-gym.
examples.en: I haven't gone to the gym in a week.

notes: 'Buwanan' = monthly; 'kada buwan' = every month; 'katapusan ng buwan' = end of the month.

examples.tl: Dalawang buwan na akong hindi nakakauwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: I haven't been home to the province in two months.

notes: 'Ilang taon ka na?' = how old are you? Answer with Spanish numbers: 'trenta y dos'. 'Taun-taon' = every year.

examples.tl: Ilang taon ka na? Trenta?
examples.en: How old are you? Thirty?

examples.tl: Dalawang taon na ako dito sa Pilipinas.
examples.en: I've been here in the Philippines for two years.

notes: Same word for day and sun. 'Araw-araw' = every day; 'buong araw' = all day; 'maaraw' = sunny.

examples.tl: Tatlong araw ang holiday, uuwi ako sa probinsya.
examples.en: The holiday is three days, I'll go home to the province.

examples.tl: Ang tirik ng araw, bitbit ka ng payong.
examples.en: The sun is blazing, bring an umbrella.

notes: 'Magandang umaga' = good morning. 'Kaninang umaga' = this morning; 'bukas ng umaga' = tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Bukas ng umaga ako mag-grocery, mas kaunti ang tao.
examples.en: I'll do groceries tomorrow morning, there are fewer people.

notes: 'Magandang hapon' = good afternoon. Note 'Hapon' with capital H = Japanese.

examples.tl: Umuulan lagi sa hapon pag tag-ulan.
examples.en: It always rains in the afternoon during rainy season.

notes: 'Magandang gabi' = good evening. 'Gabi na' = it's late at night. 'Buong gabi' = all night.

examples.tl: Gabi na, mag-Grab ka na lang pauwi.
examples.en: It's late, just take a Grab home.

notes: English 'weekend' is what people say; 'Sabado at Linggo' is the Tagalog alternative. 'Long weekend' is also used as is.

examples.tl: Sa weekend tayo mag-Tagaytay, long weekend naman.
examples.en: Let's go to Tagaytay on the weekend, it's a long weekend anyway.

notes: 'Sa susunod na' + unit = next: sa susunod na buwan, sa susunod na taon. 'Sa susunod' alone = next time.

examples.tl: Sa susunod na linggo ang move-in ko sa condo.
examples.en: My condo move-in is next week.

notes: Used alone to mean 'next time' or 'in the future'. 'Sa susunod, mag-Grab na lang tayo.'

examples.tl: Sa susunod, mag-book tayo nang maaga para mas mura.
examples.en: Next time, let's book early so it's cheaper.

notes: 'Noong nakaraang' + unit = last: noong nakaraang linggo, noong nakaraang taon. Spoken often shortened to 'last month'.

examples.tl: Noong nakaraang buwan, tumaas ang bill ng Meralco.
examples.en: Last month, the Meralco bill went up.

notes: 'Kada' (from Spanish cada) = per/every: kada buwan, kada oras, kada tao. Common for rates and prices.

examples.tl: Singkwenta kada araw ang parking sa office.
examples.en: Parking at the office is fifty per day.

notes: Reduplication = every: araw-araw, gabi-gabi (every night), linggo-linggo, buwan-buwan, taun-taon.

examples.tl: Araw-araw akong nag-jeep papuntang Ayala.
examples.en: I take the jeep to Ayala every day.

examples.tl: Linggo-linggo kaming nag-badminton sa BGC.
examples.en: We play badminton in BGC every week.

notes: 'Tuwing Lunes' = every Monday; 'tuwing umaga' = every morning; 'tuwing umuulan' = whenever it rains.

examples.tl: Tuwing Sabado, palengke ako nang maaga.
examples.en: Every Saturday, I go to the market early.

examples.tl: Baha sa amin tuwing may bagyo.
examples.en: Our area floods whenever there's a typhoon.

notes: 'Hanggang bukas' = until tomorrow; 'hanggang dito' = up to here; 'hanggang kailan?' = until when?

examples.tl: Hanggang alas-diyes lang bukas ang 7-Eleven? Hindi, 24 hours 'yon.
examples.en: Is 7-Eleven only open until ten? No, it's 24 hours.

examples.tl: Hanggang kailan ka sa Manila?
examples.en: Until when are you in Manila?

notes: 'Mula alas-otso hanggang alas-singko' = from 8 to 5. 'Mula noon' = since then. Also 'galing' for 'from (a place)'.

examples.tl: Mula Lunes hanggang Biyernes ang pasok ko.
examples.en: I work from Monday to Friday.

notes: 'Simula bukas' = starting tomorrow; 'sa simula' = at the start; 'magsimula' = to begin.

examples.tl: Simula bukas, diet na ako. Promise.
examples.en: Starting tomorrow, I'm on a diet. Promise.

en: a long time; slow to happen
notes: 'Matagal na' = it's been a long time. 'Ang tagal!' = this is taking forever! 'Matagal pa' = not for a while yet.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng Grab, bente minutes na akong naghihintay.
examples.en: The Grab is taking forever, I've been waiting twenty minutes.

examples.tl: Matagal na kaming magkaibigan.
examples.en: We've been friends a long time.

notes: Both 'easy' and 'quick'. 'Madali lang' = it's easy / it'll be quick. 'Dalian mo!' = hurry up!

examples.tl: Madali lang mag-GCash, scan lang ng QR.
examples.en: GCash is easy, just scan the QR.

examples.tl: Dalian mo, aalis na ang jeep!
examples.en: Hurry up, the jeep is leaving!

notes: 'Bilisan mo' = speed it up. 'Ang bilis!' = that was fast!

examples.tl: Ang bilis ng delivery, kahapon lang ako nag-order.
examples.en: The delivery was so fast, I only ordered yesterday.

notes: 'Ang bagal!' = so slow! Used for internet, traffic, service.

examples.tl: Ang bagal ng internet pag umuulan.
examples.en: The internet is so slow when it rains.

notes: Two uses: 'tapos' = and then (story connector); 'tapos na' = finished. Extremely frequent in spoken narration.

examples.tl: Nag-gym ako, tapos kumain, tapos natulog.
examples.en: I went to the gym, then ate, then slept.

examples.tl: Tapos na ba ang meeting?
examples.en: Is the meeting over?

notes: 'Habang naghihintay' = while waiting. 'Habang maaga' = while it's early.

examples.tl: Kain muna tayo habang naghihintay ng Grab.
examples.en: Let's eat first while waiting for the Grab.

notes: Almost always shortened to 'pag' in speech: 'pag umuulan', 'pag Biyernes'. For a question 'when?' use 'kailan'.

examples.tl: Pag umuulan, baha sa Taft.
examples.en: When it rains, Taft floods.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo ako pag nandito ka na.
examples.en: Call me when you're here.

notes: Question word only. For 'when' in a statement use 'kapag/pag' (future) or 'noong' (past). 'Kailan pa?' = since when?

examples.tl: Kailan ang flight mo pabalik ng States?
examples.en: When is your flight back to the States?

examples.tl: Kailan ka free? Dinner tayo.
examples.en: When are you free? Let's have dinner.

notes: 'Gaano ka-' + adjective = how ___. Also 'Ilang oras?' (how many hours). Taglish: 'How long ba?'

examples.tl: Gaano katagal ang biyahe papuntang airport?
examples.en: How long is the trip to the airport?

notes: Enclitic: 'Kain muna tayo' = let's eat first. 'Hindi muna' = not for now. 'Sandali muna' = wait a moment.

examples.tl: Kain muna tayo bago mag-meeting.
examples.en: Let's eat first before the meeting.

examples.tl: Dito muna ako sa Makati, baka next year lilipat.
examples.en: I'm in Makati for now, maybe I'll move next year.

examples.tl: Sa ngayon, okay pa ang budget ko.
examples.en: For now, my budget is still okay.

notes: Same word: 'bago' = new (adj) and 'bago' = before (conj). 'Bago ako umalis' = before I left.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo ako bago ka umalis.
examples.en: Call me before you leave.

examples.tl: Bago ang phone mo? Ang ganda!
examples.en: Is your phone new? Nice!

notes: Days are Spanish-derived. 'Sa Lunes' = on (this coming) Monday; 'noong Lunes' = last Monday; 'tuwing Lunes' = every Monday.

examples.tl: Ayoko ng Lunes, sobrang traffic.
examples.en: I hate Mondays, so much traffic.

examples.tl: Sa Martes ang appointment ko sa dentista.
examples.en: My dentist appointment is on Tuesday.

examples.tl: Miyerkules na, kalagitnaan na ng linggo.
examples.en: It's Wednesday already, midweek.

examples.tl: Huwebes ang payday namin ngayong buwan.
examples.en: Our payday is on Thursday this month.

notes: 'Biyernes Santo' = Good Friday, when almost everything closes.

examples.tl: Biyernes na! Inom tayo sa Poblacion mamaya.
examples.en: It's Friday! Let's drink in Poblacion later.

examples.tl: Sabado ng umaga ako nagpapalaba.
examples.en: I have my laundry done Saturday morning.

notes: Capital L = Sunday; lowercase 'linggo' = week. 'Sabado't Linggo' = the weekend.

examples.tl: Linggo ngayon, sarado ang bangko.
examples.en: It's Sunday today, the bank is closed.

notes: Months are Spanish-derived, but in Taglish most people say the English month names. Tagalog months appear on forms and in formal speech.

examples.tl: Malamig sa Baguio pag Enero.
examples.en: It's cold in Baguio in January.

examples.tl: Sa Pebrero ang Valentine's, mahal ang bulaklak.
examples.en: Valentine's is in February, flowers are expensive.

examples.tl: Nagsisimula ang tag-init sa Marso.
examples.en: The hot season starts in March.

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa Manila pag Abril.
examples.en: Manila is extremely hot in April.

notes: Mayo = May (also the brand of mayonnaise, context tells).

examples.tl: Maraming piyesta sa probinsya tuwing Mayo.
examples.en: There are many fiestas in the provinces every May.

examples.tl: Hunyo na, simula na ng tag-ulan.
examples.en: It's June, the rainy season is starting.

examples.tl: Noong Hulyo, tatlong bagyo ang dumaan.
examples.en: Last July, three typhoons passed through.

notes: Agosto = Buwan ng Wika (National Language Month) in schools.

examples.tl: Agosto ang Buwan ng Wika sa mga eskwelahan.
examples.en: August is National Language Month in schools.

notes: The 'ber months' (September to December) are the Christmas season in the Philippines.

examples.tl: Setyembre na, may Christmas songs na sa mall.
examples.en: It's September, there are Christmas songs in the mall already.

examples.tl: Oktubre ang kaarawan ko, sa a-kinse.
examples.en: My birthday is in October, on the 15th.

notes: Nov 1 = Undas (All Saints' Day); traffic out of Manila is heavy.

examples.tl: Sa Nobyembre ang Undas, uuwi kami sa probinsya.
examples.en: Undas is in November, we'll go home to the province.

examples.tl: Disyembre na, Pasko na naman!
examples.en: It's December, it's Christmas again!

notes: Dates: 'a-kinse ng Oktubre' or 'ika-15 ng Oktubre' (Oct 15). In Taglish most say 'October 15'. A romantic 'date' is just 'date'.

examples.tl: Anong petsa ang flight mo? Para ma-check ko ang schedule ko.
examples.en: What date is your flight? So I can check my schedule.

notes: Answer: 'A-onse ng Oktubre' or just 'October 11'. Also 'Anong araw ngayon?' = what day is it?

examples.tl: Anong petsa ngayon? Baka due na ang Meralco.
examples.en: What's the date today? The Meralco bill might be due.

taglish: Birthday ko sa Sabado, libre ko kayo.
notes: 'Maligayang kaarawan' = happy birthday (formal); everyone says 'Happy birthday!'. Celebrant treats the group: 'libre mo kami'.

examples.tl: Kaarawan ni Mama sa a-bente ng Nobyembre, bibili ako ng cake sa Goldilocks.
examples.en: Mom's birthday is November 20, I'll buy a cake at Goldilocks.

notes: 'Maligayang Pasko' = Merry Christmas. 'Pamasko' = Christmas gift/money. Season starts in the 'ber months'.

examples.tl: Uuwi ka ba sa States sa Pasko o dito ka lang?
examples.en: Are you going home to the States for Christmas or staying here?

notes: 'Kumusta ang panahon?' = how's the weather? 'Sa panahon ngayon' = these days. 'Panahon ko' = my time/era.

examples.tl: Ang gulo ng panahon, mainit tapos biglang uulan.
examples.en: The weather is crazy, hot then suddenly it rains.

notes: March to May. People also say 'summer'. 'Tag-araw' is the dry season in general.

examples.tl: Pag tag-init, sobrang taas ng bill sa aircon.
examples.en: In the hot season, the aircon bill is sky high.

notes: June to about November; typhoons and floods. 'Tag-' prefix = season of.

examples.tl: Tag-ulan na, dala ka lagi ng payong at extra tsinelas.
examples.en: It's rainy season, always bring an umbrella and spare slippers.

notes: December to February, when Manila drops to the low 20s C and people wear jackets. Also used for winter abroad.

examples.tl: Tag-lamig na, 22 degrees sa Manila, jacket weather!
examples.en: It's the cold season, 22 degrees in Manila, jacket weather!

notes: Noun. Verb forms: umulan (rained), umuulan (raining), uulan (will rain). 'Malakas ang ulan' = heavy rain.

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng ulan, walang Grab na tumatanggap.
examples.en: The rain is heavy, no Grab driver is accepting.

notes: Incompleted aspect of 'umulan'. 'Uulan ba mamaya?' = will it rain later? 'Umulan kanina' = it rained earlier.

examples.tl: Umuulan ba sa inyo? Dito sa Makati malakas.
examples.en: Is it raining where you are? Here in Makati it's heavy.

notes: 'Na' marks that the rain just started. What people shout before grabbing the laundry off the line.

examples.tl: Umuulan na! Dalian mo, kunin mo ang sinampay!
examples.en: It's raining! Hurry, get the laundry!

notes: From 'araw' (sun). 'Matirik ang araw' = the sun is blazing.

examples.tl: Maaraw ngayon, pwede nang magpatuyo ng labada.
examples.en: It's sunny today, the laundry can dry.

notes: Weather, food, and tempers. 'Mainit ang ulo ko' = I'm irritated. 'Ang init!' is the usual exclamation.

examples.tl: Mainit masyado sa labas, sa mall na lang tayo tumambay.
examples.en: It's too hot outside, let's just hang out at the mall.

notes: 'Ang' + root = exclamation: ang init, ang lamig, ang lakas ng ulan. Said roughly daily March to May.

examples.tl: Ang init! Parang nasa oven ang Makati ngayon.
examples.en: It's so hot! Makati feels like an oven today.

notes: Weather, drinks, aircon. 'Malamig na tubig' = cold water. 'Nilalamig ako' = I feel cold.

examples.tl: Malamig sa Tagaytay, dalhin mo ang jacket mo.
examples.en: It's cold in Tagaytay, bring your jacket.

notes: Opposite: 'Naiinitan ako' = I feel hot. Common complaint in over-aircon'd offices and buses.

examples.tl: Nilalamig ako sa office, sobrang lakas ng aircon.
examples.en: I'm cold at the office, the aircon is too strong.

notes: 'Malakas ang hangin' = the wind is strong. Also 'hangin' = air, and slang 'hangin' = full of hot air.

examples.tl: Malakas ang hangin, baka may bagyong paparating.
examples.en: The wind is strong, maybe a typhoon is coming.

examples.tl: Mahangin sa Baywalk sa gabi, presko.
examples.en: It's windy at Baywalk at night, refreshing.

notes: Typhoons get local names (Ondoy, Yolanda, Carina). 'May bagyo' = there's a typhoon. 'Signal no. 1-5' are PAGASA warning levels.

examples.tl: May bagyo daw sa Linggo, mag-stock na tayo ng tubig.
examples.en: They say there's a typhoon on Sunday, let's stock up on water.

taglish: Signal no. 2 na sa Metro Manila, walang pasok.
notes: PAGASA wind signals 1 to 5. Signal 2 or 3 in Metro Manila usually means classes and government work are suspended.

examples.tl: Signal no. 2 na sa Maynila, suspended na ang klase.
examples.en: Signal number 2 in Manila now, classes are suspended.

notes: 'Pasok' = going in (to work or school). Announced during typhoons and holidays. 'May pasok ba bukas?' = is there work/school tomorrow?

examples.tl: Walang pasok bukas, signal no. 3!
examples.en: No work or school tomorrow, signal number 3!
examples.taglish: Walang pasok bukas, yes! Netflix all day.

notes: 'Bumaha' = it flooded; 'binaha' = got flooded; 'baha sa España' = España is flooded. 'Hanggang tuhod' = knee-deep.

examples.tl: Baha na sa Taft, hanggang tuhod daw.
examples.en: Taft is flooded, knee-deep they say.

notes: From 'ulap' (cloud). 'Makulimlim' = gloomy/overcast, more literary.

examples.tl: Maulap ngayon, mukhang uulan mamaya.
examples.en: It's cloudy today, looks like it'll rain later.

notes: 'Umaambon' = it's drizzling. 'Ambon lang' = just a drizzle, no need for an umbrella.

examples.tl: Ambon lang, kaya pa maglakad hanggang MRT.
examples.en: It's just a drizzle, we can still walk to the MRT.

notes: Stress matters: ba-SA = wet; BA-sa = read. 'Nabasa ako' = I got wet. 'Basang-basa' = soaking wet.

examples.tl: Basang-basa ako, nahuli ako ng ulan sa labas ng MRT.
examples.en: I'm soaking wet, I got caught in the rain outside the MRT.

notes: Stress matters: tu-YO = dry; TU-yo = dried fish (breakfast staple). 'Tuyo na ang labada' = the laundry is dry.

examples.tl: Tuyo na ba ang damit? Isusuot ko mamaya.
examples.en: Are the clothes dry yet? I'll wear them later.

notes: The sticky heat before a storm. Many just say 'humid' or 'sobrang init'. 'Alinsangan' = humidity.

examples.tl: Maalinsangan ngayon, parang uulan mamaya.
examples.en: It's muggy today, feels like it'll rain later.

notes: 'Kidlat' = lightning. 'Kumukulog' = it's thundering. 'Kulog at kidlat' = thunder and lightning.

examples.tl: Ang lakas ng kulog, natakot ang aso.
examples.en: The thunder is so loud, the dog got scared.

notes: 'Kumikidlat' = there's lightning. Also slang for someone very fast.

examples.tl: May kidlat, wag ka munang mag-swimming.
examples.en: There's lightning, don't go swimming yet.

notes: Used for sun and rain. 'May payong ka?' is a daily question in tag-ulan.

examples.tl: Dala ka ng payong, baka umulan mamayang hapon.
examples.en: Bring an umbrella, it might rain this afternoon.

notes: 'Lumindol' = there was an earthquake. 'Nilindol ba kayo?' = did you feel the quake? Phivolcs reports intensity.

examples.tl: Lumindol kanina! Naramdaman mo ba sa condo?
examples.en: There was an earthquake earlier! Did you feel it in the condo?

taglish: Brownout sa amin, walang aircon, init!
notes: Filipinos say 'brownout' for any power outage. 'Walang kuryente' = no electricity. 'Bumalik na ang kuryente' = power is back.

examples.tl: Brownout sa buong barangay kagabi dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: The whole barangay had a power outage last night because of the typhoon.

notes: 'Anong kulay?' = what color? 'Kulay pula' = red-colored. 'Makulay' = colorful.

examples.tl: Anong kulay ng kotse ng Grab? Puti daw.
examples.en: What color is the Grab car? White, they say.

notes: Useful shopping and Grab-spotting question. Answer with the color word alone: 'Itim.'

examples.tl: Anong kulay ang gusto mo, itim o puti?
examples.en: What color do you want, black or white?

notes: 'Mapula' = reddish. Red taxis and red jeeps are common sights.

examples.tl: Pulang jeep ang sakyan mo, 'yung may sign na Guadalupe.
examples.en: Take the red jeep, the one with the Guadalupe sign.

notes: 'Maputi' = fair-skinned, often used as a compliment. 'Puting damit' = white clothes.

examples.tl: Puting Vios ang Grab, plate na nagtatapos sa 88.
examples.en: The Grab is a white Vios, plate ending in 88.

notes: 'Maitim' = dark-skinned. 'Itim na kape' = black coffee.

examples.tl: Itim na lang ang bibilhin ko, hindi madumi.
examples.en: I'll just buy black, it doesn't look dirty.

notes: 'Blue' is said just as often. 'Bughaw' is the purist word, rarely spoken.

examples.tl: Asul ang uniform ng guard sa condo namin.
examples.en: The guards' uniform at our condo is blue.

notes: 'Green' is equally common. 'Berdeng biro' = a dirty joke. 'Luntian' is literary.

examples.tl: Pag berde na ang ilaw, tumawid ka na.
examples.en: When the light is green, cross.

notes: Yellow taxis in Manila are the airport taxis (more expensive). 'Dilaw' also has political connotations (Aquino party).

examples.tl: Wag ka sumakay sa dilaw na taxi, mas mahal 'yon.
examples.en: Don't take the yellow taxi, that one is more expensive.

notes: Almost everyone says 'orange'. 'Kahel' is the textbook word; you'll see it on forms and in school.

examples.tl: Orange ang shirt ng rider, 'yung Shopee delivery.
examples.en: The rider's shirt is orange, the Shopee delivery one.

notes: 'Violet' is the common spoken word. 'Ube' (purple yam) is used to describe that shade too.

examples.tl: Violet ang paborito niyang kulay, kaya ube lahat ng gamit niya.
examples.en: Violet is her favorite color, so all her stuff is ube-colored.

notes: 'Rosas' = pink and also the rose flower. 'Pink' is more common in speech. 'Kulay rosas' = pink-colored.

examples.tl: Pink ang helmet ng Angkas rider ko kanina.
examples.en: My Angkas rider's helmet earlier was pink.

notes: Mostly used for skin tone with pride ('kayumangging Pilipino'). For objects people say 'brown'.

examples.tl: Kayumanggi ang kutis ng Pilipino, ipagmalaki mo.
examples.en: Filipinos have brown skin, be proud of it.

notes: English 'gray' is what people say; 'abo' means ash, so 'kulay-abo' = ash-colored.

examples.tl: Gray ang building namin, 'yung katabi ng 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Our building is gray, the one next to 7-Eleven.

notes: For lighting and shades: 'madilim na kulay' = dark color; 'madilim na' = it's dark already (evening).

examples.tl: Madilim na, umuwi na tayo.
examples.en: It's dark already, let's go home.

notes: Lighting, and also 'clear' as in 'maliwanag ba?' = is that clear/understood?

examples.tl: Maliwanag pa, pwede pa tayong mag-jogging sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: It's still bright, we can still jog at Ayala Triangle.

notes: 'Maraming tao' = many people; 'marami pa' = there's still a lot; 'maraming salamat' = thanks a lot. 'Ang dami!' = so many!

examples.tl: Maraming tao sa MRT pag alas-sais ng hapon.
examples.en: There are a lot of people on the MRT at six in the evening.

examples.tl: Ang dami ng ulam, hindi ko mauubos.
examples.en: There's so much food, I can't finish it.

notes: 'Kaunti' is the standard spelling; 'konti' is how it's said. 'Konti lang' = just a bit. 'Kaunting tubig' = a little water.

examples.tl: Konti lang ang kanin ko, diet ako.
examples.en: Just a little rice for me, I'm on a diet.

examples.tl: Konti lang ang tao sa mall pag Lunes ng umaga.
examples.en: There are few people at the mall on Monday mornings.

notes: 'Sobra' = too much/leftover; 'sobrang' + adj = very/extremely: sobrang mahal, sobrang init. 'Sobra na!' = that's too much!

examples.tl: Sobra ang sukli, kuya, binigyan mo ako ng bente imbes na diyes.
examples.en: The change is too much, kuya, you gave me twenty instead of ten.

examples.tl: Sobrang traffic kanina, dalawang oras ako sa EDSA.
examples.en: Traffic was terrible earlier, two hours on EDSA.

notes: 'Kulang ang bayad' = payment is short; 'kulang sa tulog' = short on sleep; 'kulang pa ng isa' = one more needed.

examples.tl: Kulang ng singko ang bayad mo, kuya.
examples.en: Your payment is five pesos short, kuya.

examples.tl: Kulang ako sa tulog, alas-dos ako natulog.
examples.en: I'm short on sleep, I slept at two.

notes: 'Sapat na' = that's enough. In speech 'enough na' or 'okay na' is also common. Opposite: 'kulang'.

examples.tl: Sapat na ang isang libo para sa grocery ng isang linggo? Hindi na, mahal na lahat.
examples.en: Is a thousand enough for a week's groceries? Not anymore, everything's expensive.

notes: Stress matters: pu-NO = full; PU-no = tree. 'Puno na ang jeep' = the jeep is full. 'Punuin mo' = fill it up. 'Busog' = full (stomach).

examples.tl: Puno na ang jeep, hintay tayo ng susunod.
examples.en: The jeep is full, let's wait for the next one.

notes: Literally 'has no contents'. 'Walang laman ang ref' = the fridge is empty. 'Walang laman ang GCash ko' = my GCash is empty.

examples.tl: Walang laman ang GCash ko, pa-load muna ako sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: My GCash is empty, I'll top up at 7-Eleven first.

notes: Market prices are per kilo: 'magkano ang kilo?' Use Tagalog numbers + linker: isang kilo, dalawang kilo, kalahating kilo.

examples.tl: Magkano ang kilo ng bangus, ate?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of bangus, ate?

examples.tl: Isang kilo ng baboy, 'yung may taba.
examples.en: One kilo of pork, the part with fat.

notes: Model for number + linker + unit: tatlong kilo, limang kilo, kalahating kilo.

examples.tl: Dalawang kilo ng bigas, tapos isang supot ng sibuyas.
examples.en: Two kilos of rice, then one bag of onions.

notes: 'Dalawang daang gramo' = 200 grams; in practice people say 'two hundred grams' or 'quarter kilo' (kapat).

examples.tl: Dalawang daang gramo lang ng keso, para sa isang tao lang.
examples.en: Just 200 grams of cheese, it's just for one person.

notes: Gas and water: 'isang litro', 'limang litro ng tubig' (the refill jug). Taglish 'liter' also fine.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang gasolina, singkwenta y singko kada litro.
examples.en: Gas went up again, fifty-five per liter.

notes: Also 'metro' = taxi meter ('metro lang, kuya' = use the meter). 'Limang metro' = five meters.

examples.tl: Metro lang, kuya, wag fixed price.
examples.en: Just use the meter, kuya, no fixed price.

examples.tl: Mga sampung metro lang ang layo ng 7-Eleven sa gate.
examples.en: The 7-Eleven is only about ten meters from the gate.

notes: Taglish often 'kilometers' or 'km'. 'Ilang kilometro?' = how many kilometers?

examples.tl: Limang kilometro lang pero isang oras ang biyahe dahil sa traffic.
examples.en: Only five kilometers but the trip takes an hour because of traffic.

notes: Counter for items sold individually: 'limang piraso ng pandesal'. Also 'pira-piraso' = in pieces. Taglish 'pieces' is common too.

examples.tl: Tatlong piraso ng siopao, ate, asado.
examples.en: Three pieces of siopao, ate, asado.

notes: 'Isa lang' also works. 'Tig-isang piraso' = one piece each.

examples.tl: Isang piraso lang ng mangga, pang-isahan lang.
examples.en: Just one piece of mango, it's just for one person.

taglish: Isang pack ng Marlboro at isang Coke.
notes: English 'pack' is the everyday word at sari-sari stores and groceries; 'pakete' is the Tagalog form, less used.

examples.tl: Dalawang pack ng pancit canton, 'yung extra hot.
examples.en: Two packs of pancit canton, the extra hot one.

notes: 'Isang bote ng tubig'. 'Bote-bote' = bottle after bottle. Bottle deposits are a thing: 'ibalik ang bote'.

examples.tl: Isang bote ng malamig na tubig, please.
examples.en: One bottle of cold water, please.

examples.tl: Ilang bote ng Red Horse ang inubos niyo kagabi?
examples.en: How many bottles of Red Horse did you finish last night?

notes: 'De-lata' = canned goods (corned beef, sardines). 'Isang lata ng Coke'.

examples.tl: Mag-stock tayo ng de-lata, baka bumaha ulit.
examples.en: Let's stock up on canned goods, it might flood again.

notes: 'Supot' = the small plastic or paper bag from a store or palengke. 'Pa-supot' = please bag it. 'Bag' for handbags.

examples.tl: Pa-supot po, ate, wala akong eco bag.
examples.en: Please bag it, ate, I don't have an eco bag.

examples.tl: Isang supot ng sibuyas at isang supot ng bawang.
examples.en: One bag of onions and one bag of garlic.

notes: Palengke vendors sell tomatoes, chilies, kalamansi by the 'tumpok' at a fixed price: 'bente isang tumpok'.

examples.tl: Magkano isang tumpok ng kamatis? Bente? Sige, dalawang tumpok.
examples.en: How much for a pile of tomatoes? Twenty? Okay, two piles.

notes: 'Piso' = one peso / pesos in Tagalog counting: 'limang piso' (but people say 'singko'). 'Piso lang' = only a peso. 'Pera' = money.

examples.tl: Piso lang ang dagdag sa pamasahe? Ok lang 'yan.
examples.en: Only a one-peso fare increase? That's fine.

examples.tl: Isang daang piso ang entrance, pero libre ang bata.
examples.en: Entrance is one hundred pesos, but kids are free.

notes: Price question. Answer in Spanish numbers: 'Bente', 'Singkwenta', 'Dos syentos'. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much altogether? 'Ilan' is for counting, not price.

examples.tl: Magkano 'to, ate? Pwedeng tawad?
examples.en: How much is this, ate? Can I haggle?

examples.tl: Magkano ang isang kilo ng manok ngayon? Dos syentos? Ang mahal!
examples.en: How much is a kilo of chicken now? Two hundred? So expensive!

notes: Prefix for 'each/apiece': tig-bente = twenty each, tig-isa = one each, tig-dalawa = two each. 'Tig-isa tayo' = one each.

examples.tl: Tig-bente ang siomai, tatlo para singkwenta.
examples.en: Siomai are twenty each, three for fifty.

examples.tl: Tig-isa na lang tayo ng beer, may pasok bukas.
examples.en: Let's just have one beer each, there's work tomorrow.

notes: 'Bawat isa' = each one; 'bawat tao' = every person. 'Kada' is the casual equivalent for rates.

examples.tl: Bawat isa may dalang ulam, potluck tayo.
examples.en: Each one brings a dish, let's potluck.

notes: 'Buong araw' = all day; 'buong linggo' = the whole week; 'buong manok' = a whole chicken. 'Buo pa' = still intact.

examples.tl: Buong araw akong nasa bahay dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: I was home all day because of the typhoon.

examples.tl: Isang buong manok, 'yung inihaw.
examples.en: One whole chicken, the roasted one.

notes: Root of 'marami'. 'Ang dami!' = so many! 'Gaano kadami?' = how many/how much? 'Dami mo namang satsat' = you talk so much.

examples.tl: Ang dami ng tao sa Divisoria, Pasko na nga.
examples.en: There are so many people in Divisoria, it's Christmas season after all.

notes: The everyday intensifier: sobrang init, sobrang mahal, sobrang late. Also 'super' in Taglish: 'super traffic'.

examples.tl: Sobrang init ngayon, 38 degrees daw.
examples.en: It's extremely hot today, 38 degrees they say.

examples.tl: Sobrang mahal ng renta sa BGC.
examples.en: Rent in BGC is super expensive.

notes: From Spanish 'medio'. Softens anything: medyo late, medyo mahal, medyo malayo. Used constantly.

examples.tl: Medyo late ako, mga alas-siyete ako makakarating.
examples.en: I'm a bit late, I'll get there around seven.

examples.tl: Medyo malamig ngayon, Disyembre na nga.
examples.en: It's kind of cold today, it's December after all.

notes: 'Masyadong mahal' = too expensive; 'masyado ka naman' = you're too much. Follows or precedes the adjective: 'mainit masyado'.

examples.tl: Masyadong maaga ang alas-singko, alas-sais na lang.
examples.en: Five is too early, let's make it six instead.

examples.tl: Masyadong mahal ang mangga ngayon, hindi pa season.
examples.en: Mangoes are too expensive right now, it's not the season yet.

notes: Both intensifier and reaction: 'Talaga?' = really? 'Mainit talaga' = it's really hot. 'Talagang' before an adjective.

examples.tl: Talaga? Walang pasok bukas?
examples.en: Really? No work tomorrow?

examples.tl: Mahal talaga ang bilihin ngayon.
examples.en: Prices are really high these days.

notes: 'Halos araw-araw' = almost every day; 'halos lahat' = almost everyone/everything; 'halos isang oras' = almost an hour.

examples.tl: Halos araw-araw umuulan sa Agosto.
examples.en: It rains almost every day in August.

examples.tl: Halos isang oras ang pila sa LTO.
examples.en: The line at the LTO was almost an hour.

notes: Comparative marker: mas mura = cheaper, mas mabilis = faster, mas maaga = earlier. 'Mas gusto ko' = I prefer. From Spanish 'mas'.

examples.tl: Mas mura sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.
examples.en: It's cheaper at the market than at the supermarket.

examples.tl: Mas mabilis ang Angkas kaysa sa Grab pag rush hour.
examples.en: Angkas is faster than Grab during rush hour.

notes: Superlative prefix: pinakamura = cheapest, pinakamabilis = fastest, pinakamainit = hottest. 'Pinaka-' + English works too: pinaka-busy.

examples.tl: Abril ang pinakamainit na buwan sa Manila.
examples.en: April is the hottest month in Manila.

examples.tl: Ito ang pinakamurang kilo ng bigas dito.
examples.en: This is the cheapest kilo of rice here.

notes: Prefix intensifier: napakainit, napakamahal, napakatagal. Slightly more emphatic/formal than 'sobrang'; both are common.

examples.tl: Napakatagal ng pila sa NAIA immigration kanina.
examples.en: The line at NAIA immigration earlier was extremely long.

notes: 'Ulit' after a verb = again: 'sabihin mo ulit' = say it again. 'Ulitin' = to repeat. 'Paulit-ulit' = over and over.

examples.tl: Umulan ulit, pangatlong beses ngayong araw.
examples.en: It rained again, third time today.

examples.tl: Pakisabi ulit, hindi ko narinig.
examples.en: Please say it again, I didn't hear.

notes: 'Biglang umulan' = it suddenly rained. 'Biglaan' = last-minute/sudden (plans). 'Nabigla ako' = I was caught off guard.

examples.tl: Biglang umulan kanina, maaraw pa kanina-kanina lang.
examples.en: It suddenly rained earlier, it was sunny just a moment before.

examples.tl: Biglaan ang inuman, kaya hindi ako nakapunta.
examples.en: The drinking session was last-minute, so I couldn't go.

notes: From Spanish 'veces'. 'Ilang beses?' = how many times? 'Dalawang beses' = twice; 'unang beses' = first time; 'minsan' = once.

examples.tl: Tatlong beses na akong nag-Palawan, hindi pa ako nagsasawa.
examples.en: I've been to Palawan three times and I'm not tired of it yet.

examples.tl: Ilang beses ka kumakain sa labas kada linggo?
examples.en: How many times do you eat out per week?

notes: Short follow-up question, typically about traffic, rain, or prices. Answer: 'Oo, lagi' or 'Minsan lang'.

examples.tl: Ganito ba lagi ang traffic sa EDSA? Oo, lalo na pag Biyernes.
examples.en: Is EDSA traffic always like this? Yes, especially on Fridays.
